Hi Lena / Tom —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposals so we can lock the POC scope and avoid last-minute surprises: 

1) High-level ask (your priority): low-latency extraction + rerank for 10M monthly queries, with structured tool outputs for downstream workflows.
2) Target SLA: 200ms 95th on token generation for interactive flows; batch rerank can be 500–800ms.
3) Auth model: you indicated internal apps will call Redwood via a service account from within GCP; procurement also asked about SSO for human users.

Immediate engineering items (owners + proposed due dates):
- Provide minimal dev sandbox access + example CPI keys (Redwood): marissa_cole — due 2028-12-07
- Tool definitions: we propose shipping a canonical tool-def JSON and a small helper SDK for function/tool calling (see attached example). Sean to review compatibility with your tool endpoints.
- Auth & routing: Karthik to propose 2 routing options (region-first vs cost-first) with fallback to a quantized variant. Karthik — due 2028-12-06.
- Embeddings/reranker: confirm corpus size and accepted vector dimensions; Tom to share sample dataset by 2028-12-08.

Attachments: skybridge_requirements.xlsx (your spreadsheet), redwood_tool-def-examples.json (sample tool definitions + error semantics).

Next meeting: propose Thu 2028-12-07 16:00 PT to walk the SDK quickstart and run through an auth demo. Please confirm.

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear notes. Confirming a few items from our side: 

- We can share a 10k-row sample of our transaction logs and the current embed vectors by Friday (Tom is on it). Expect the file to be ~120MB.
- For auth: service account for server-to-server calls is preferred. For the internal UI we do want SSO (Okta). Can Redwood support both and map human actions to an audit_id?
- Tooling: the tool-def semantics look good; critical for us is idempotency and explicit error types so our orchestrator can retry/skip.

Two questions before the call: 
1) SDK language support — we use Node (backend), Python (data team), and a small Java service. Can you confirm SDKs for those or an HTTP-first approach?
2) In the tool examples you reference parallel tool calls for resilience; can you share recommended fanout limits and guidance on partial failures?

We'd like to keep the POC surface small: implement the extraction tool + a reranker prototype (embedding store will be separate). If that looks good, procurement will move to an SOW.

Best,
Lena

Subject: Re: SkyBridge POC: tooling decisions, auth & routing next steps

Folks — adding a quick engineering note on tradeoffs and an initial recommendation for the POC: 

1) SDK / HTTP: we’ll ship a Node + Python SDK in the sandbox. Java is lower-priority; recommend HTTP-first (signed requests) so the Java service can call without a native SDK in POC.

2) Tool definition & error taxonomy: the attached JSON shows 3 error classes we recommend: transient (retry with backoff), soft-fail (return null + operator review), and terminal (bubble up to user). Include request_id and attempt_count in every tool response.

3) Parallel tool calls: for extraction + enrichment we suggest a conservative fanout of 3 parallel tool calls per request for POC (timeouts 500ms per tool). On partial failures: return partial structured payload + a tools.errors array with the classification. Our SDK will include a small orchestrator helper that launches parallel calls and aggregates results with a configurable quorum.

4) Auth: support service account bearer tokens for server calls and OIDC flow for human users. Audit mapping: Redwood will propagate X-Redwood-Audit-Id header if present; otherwise we suggest injecting an audit_id at the proxy layer. 

I attached the draft tool-def and an example aggregator pseudo-code snippet. Happy to tighten after we review your sample dataset.

— Sean
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
